prompt.context: Your client is the mayor of Your Town, USA. The population is 500K and declining. The economy is stagnant.
prompt.question: The mayor has asked you to help him formulate his 100 Day Plan. How can the mayor revitalize Your Town's economy and drive population growth?

clarifying_info.q: What is the age distribution of the population?
clarifying_info.a: The population ranges from ages 0 to 80, with an approximately equal number of people in each age group.

clarifying_info.q: What is the current unemployment rate?
What is the current population growth rate?
clarifying_info.a: The population is currently growing at 5% per year.

clarifying_info.q: What is the average size of a new business in terms of employees?

clarifying_info.a: The working age range is between 17 and 65 (flexible; 20-60 is also acceptable).

exhibits.shows: An exhibit from the case page; likely contains contextual data about Your Town, USA

framework: Social factors: cultural stagnation, housing affordability, school quality, crime rate
Political factors: high taxes, unfavorable laws
Economic factors: layoffs, insufficient jobs, high cost of living, unsustainable major industries
Demographic/Population factors: aging population, low birth rate, labor force mismatch with industry needs

questions.prompt: What information do you need to determine the efforts for revitalization? Brainstorm reasons for the problem in buckets.
questions.guidance: Candidate should organize reasons into buckets: Social (cultural stagnation, unaffordable housing, poor schools, high crime); Political (high taxes, unfavorable laws); Economic (layoffs, lack of jobs, high cost of living, unsustainable industries); Population (aging, low birth rate, labor force mismatch); Environmental (natural disasters, pollution).

questions.prompt: The mayor is concerned about unemployment. How many new businesses would need to open in Your Town in the next year to make the unemployment rate move from 8% to 5%, while maintaining current 5% population growth? First, state your assumptions, then calculate.
questions.guidance: Candidate should state assumptions about population age range and working-age range, then calculate the working population, current unemployed count, and the number of businesses needed. Strong answer uses Option 1 or Option 2 math below and arrives at approximately 47 businesses.

math.setup: Population = 500K, ages 0-80 uniform. Working ages 17-65. Unemployment now = 8%. Target unemployment = 5%. Population growth = 5%. Average business employs 500 people.
steps: Option 2 (alternative): Assume 4 equal age bands of 125K each (0-20, 20-40, 40-60, 60-80); working bands are 20-40 and 40-60 = 250K working population
Population next year = 525K; working pop next year = 525K * (40/80) = 262.5K ≈ 262.5K
math.answer: Approximately 47 businesses (Option 1) or approximately 39 businesses (Option 2), depending on working-age assumption. Key insight: many large businesses must open; this is one lever but not the only one.

questions.prompt: What other ideas could improve the town's economy and increase the population?
questions.guidance: Candidate should revisit the Phase 1 buckets and generate feasible solutions: invest in schools and culture to retain younger working population; appeal to industries that match the skill sets of the existing labor force; attract new businesses; improve public services and housing affordability.

questions.prompt: It turns out that a major company in the town laid off a lot of workers. Why would a company lay off workers, and what specifically should the town do to remedy the jobs lost?
questions.guidance: Reasons for layoffs: competitive pressures from rival cities; company in financial decline; company chose to expand in a lower-labor-cost market; a substitute product eroded market share. Remedies: appeal to another company in the same or similar industry to open a plant or office in Your Town; offer incentives (tax breaks, infrastructure support) to attract replacement employers.

brainstorming.prompt: What other ideas could improve the town's economy and increase the population?

categories.name: Social
ideas: Invest in public schools to retain young families
Develop cultural amenities (arts, entertainment) to reduce stagnation
Reduce crime through community policing and social programs

categories.name: Political
ideas: Offer tax incentives to attract new businesses
Reform unfavorable zoning or business regulations

categories.name: Economic
ideas: Appeal to industries that match the labor force skill set
Attract a replacement anchor employer after major layoffs
Support small business development and entrepreneurship
Develop job training programs to close labor-force skill gaps

categories.name: Population/Demographic
ideas: Attract universities or colleges to bring in young people
Create affordable housing for young workers

categories.name: Environmental
ideas: Clean up pollution to improve quality of life
Invest in green infrastructure as an economic attractor

recommendation: Open approximately 47 new businesses (each employing ~500 people) over the next year to reduce unemployment from 8% to 5% while absorbing 5% population growth
Prioritize attracting a replacement anchor employer in the same or adjacent industry as the company that laid off workers
Invest in schools, culture, and housing affordability to retain and attract the young working-age population
risks: Attracting 47 large businesses in one year is an ambitious target and may not be achievable in the short term
Population growth projections may not materialize if quality-of-life issues are not addressed simultaneously
Relying on a single industry replacement leaves the town vulnerable to further economic shocks
next_steps: Conduct a detailed audit of the town's industry mix and identify target sectors for recruitment
Develop an incentive package (tax breaks, infrastructure investment) to attract new employers
Launch a community investment program focused on schools, public safety, and cultural development
Track unemployment and population metrics quarterly against the 100 Day Plan milestones
